notes: All textures are original procedural output (numpy + Pillow); no input images, downloads or generative models.

Colour textures: RGB is sRGB-encoded and STRAIGHT (not premultiplied) with colour bled into transparent texels so bilinear/mip filtering does not fringe; multiply by A in the material for additive/premultiplied use.
Data textures (Temp, 6-way, noise, masks, LUTs) must be imported with sRGB OFF.
Flipbook frames carry a transparent border; no frame content reaches its cell edge, so mips down to ~1/8 are free of neighbour bleed.
Frame order is row-major from the top-left, the Niagara SubUV convention.

textures.name: T_VFX_AshFlakes_4x4

cells.all: 16 distinct torn flakes, charcoal (2/3) and pale grey ash (1/3)

textures.channels_desc: RGB = burnt-paper albedo (straight, bled); A = flake mask

niagara.renderer: Sprite, random SubUV, random rotation; 3D spin via Rotation Rate
niagara.material: Lit translucent/masked; colour tint from fire proximity (lerp to dark red near flames via Fire_Temp)

textures.name: T_VFX_Blackbody_LUT_256x4

layout.sample: V=0.5 (4 identical rows to satisfy minimum height); Clamp, Bilinear, NoMipmaps

textures.channels_desc: RGB = sRGB tone-mapped blackbody colour (true Planck chromaticity, compressed radiance); A (linear) = relative emissive multiplier / 4

niagara.material: u = Fire_Temp.R * Heat; Emissive = LUT.rgb * (LUT.a*4) * EmissiveScale

textures.name: T_VFX_BlueNoise_128
textures.channels_desc: single channel, rank-uniform high-pass noise (void-and-cluster approximation via iterative FFT high-pass + rank remap)

niagara.material: Dithered opacity (Masked) for soft particles, temporal dithering of dissolve

textures.name: T_VFX_DustPuff_6x6

layout.uv_note: 2048/6 = 341.33: frames are placed at round(i*341.333) and are 341 px; Unreal's SubUV cell is 341.33 px so drift is <0.7 px. Every frame has >=14 px of empty border.

textures.channels_desc: RGB = dust lit from above (baked, tan-grey albedo); A = opacity. Expanding hemispherical puff that thins out.

niagara.renderer: Sprite (1-3 per impact, ground-aligned origin at bottom-centre of the puff), lifetime ~1.2 s @ 30 fps
niagara.material: Colour = tex.rgb * SurfaceTint (sample ground albedo colour for fist-on-dirt vs stone dust); Opacity = tex.a; soft-particle depth fade 15 cm

textures.name: T_VFX_Embers_4x4

cells.8-11: spark streaks, head at +X (align to velocity)
cells.12-15: one ember cooling hot->dark (use as SubUV over lifetime)

textures.channels_desc: RGB = blackbody colour (straight); A = coverage

niagara.renderer: Sprite (random SubUV 0-7) / Sprite velocity-aligned for 8-11 / Ribbon-free
niagara.subuv: Niagara SubUV Image Index: Random 0..7 for dots; Linear 12..15 over Age for cooling
niagara.material: Additive, emissive = rgb*a*EmissiveScale (10-40), flicker with per-particle sin(Age) multiplier

textures.name: T_VFX_Fire_Color_8x8

layout.uv_note: cell = atlas/8 exactly; 6% transparent border per cell

textures.channels_desc: RGB = baked blackbody flame colour (straight, bled into transparent texels); A = flame opacity/density

niagara.subuv: Niagara SubUV Animation, 8x8, Linear blend, loop over particle Age/LoopDuration
niagara.material: M_VFX_Fire: Emissive = tex.rgb * tex.a * EmissiveScale (HDR 4-30 for bloom); Opacity = tex.a for translucent variant
niagara.sprite: Facing=camera, vertical-up aligned, size ~ (width 0.6 x height 1.0) of flame height; per-particle random start frame offset

textures.generator: vfx_fire.flame_field (curl-warped looping fBm erosion + blackbody ramp)

textures.name: T_VFX_Fire_Temp_8x8

layout.uv_note: cell = atlas/8 exactly; 6% transparent border per cell

textures.channels_desc: R = normalised temperature (0=850 K .. 1=2350 K); G = density; B = soot (cool dark smoke inside flame); A = hot-core mask

niagara.subuv: same SubUV params as Fire_Color (shared frame index)
niagara.material: Sample R, remap by (particle heat * k), look up T_VFX_Blackbody_LUT (U=R) for HDR colour; multiply LUT.A*4 as emissive intensity; use G as opacity, lerp toward black by B for soot. Lets one texture serve embers-to-white-hot flames and colour-graded fire (green/blue spell fire).

textures.name: T_VFX_Fireball_Core_4x4

layout.orientation: head (sphere) at +U/right, flame streams toward -U; rotate sprite to velocity

textures.channels_desc: RGB = blackbody colour (straight); A = density

niagara.material: Additive emissive; spawn a point light of the same colour (intensity ~ 3000-8000 cd) from the same emitter

textures.name: T_VFX_Fireball_Core_Temp_4x4

layout.orientation: head (sphere) at +U/right, flame streams toward -U; rotate sprite to velocity

textures.channels_desc: R temperature, G density, B soot, A hot core (same encoding as Fire_Temp)

niagara.material: Blackbody LUT lookup for coloured (arcane/blue) fireball variants

textures.name: T_VFX_Fireball_Trail

layout.u_axis: along ribbon (pan toward tail via UV.x -= Time*Speed)

textures.channels_desc: RGB = blackbody colour; A = density. Tileable in U, constant along length (taper/fade in material using ribbon normalised age).

niagara.renderer: Ribbon, UV0 distribution = Tiled over Length (tile distance ~ 1 texture per 2*width), Facing=camera
niagara.material: Opacity = tex.a * (1-NormalizedAge)^1.5 * edge fade; pan U for flow; Width over life 1->0.15

textures.name: T_VFX_Fireball_Trail_Temp
textures.channels_desc: R temperature, G density, B soot, A hot core

niagara.material: Blackbody LUT lookup; cool the trail along ribbon age by subtracting age*0.6 from R

textures.name: T_VFX_Gradients_256x16

layout.sample: V = (row+0.5)/16, U = normalised value / age; Wrap=Clamp, filter=Bilinear, NoMipmaps

textures.channels_desc: each row is one scalar curve replicated in RGB; A=1

niagara.material: Cheap curve lookup in materials / Niagara texture sample (age fade, attack-decay, flicker hold)

textures.name: T_VFX_HitFlash_6x6

layout.uv_note: 2048/6 = 341.33: frames are placed at round(i*341.333) and are 341 px; Unreal's SubUV cell is 341.33 px so drift is <0.7 px. Every frame has >=14 px of empty border.

textures.channels_desc: RGB = blackbody flash/spark colour; A = coverage. Frame 0-5 white-hot core+starburst, then shock ring and ballistic sparks.

niagara.renderer: Sprite (1 particle per hit, lifetime 0.6 s @ 60 fps), random Rotation + mirror U
niagara.subuv: SubUV 6x6, Linear blend OFF (flash wants crisp frames) or ON for smoothness
niagara.material: Additive emissive, EmissiveScale 8-20; scale sword hits 1.0, fist hits 0.55 + desaturate via LUT

textures.name: T_VFX_MagicGlow_2x2
textures.channels_desc: single-channel linear intensity; tint in material (any colour: heal=green, arcane=blue, pickup=gold)

niagara.subuv: Image Index chosen per emitter (no animation)
niagara.material: Emissive = tex.r * ColourHDR; Opacity = tex.r for translucent

textures.name: T_VFX_NoisePack_A_512
textures.channels_desc: R = Perlin fBm (6 oct, 4 cells), G = 1-Worley F1 (8 cells), B = Worley F2-F1 cell edges, A = Perlin-Worley (cloud base remap)

niagara.material: Erosion/dissolve masks, smoke detail, sprite UV distortion, Perlin-Worley for billowy opacity

textures.name: T_VFX_NoisePack_B_512
textures.channels_desc: R = curl vx, G = curl vy (0.5 +/- 0.5*v/vmax, subtract 0.5 and *2 to recover), B = |curl| normalised, A = scalar potential (fBm 4 oct)

niagara.material: Flow-map/advection: UV += (RG*2-1)*Strength; Niagara Sample Texture for curl forces in particles (sampled as 2D field wrapped over world XY)

textures.name: T_VFX_NoisePack_C_512
textures.channels_desc: R = ridged turbulence, G = 1-Worley F1 (6 large cells), B = 1-Worley F1 (24 small cells), A = Worley cell random id

niagara.material: Per-cell random (A) for sparkle/flicker, ridged R for lightning/magic veins, Worley for embers/bubbles

textures.name: T_VFX_Smoke_6Way_A_8x8
textures.channels_desc: R = light from +X (right), G = light from -X (left), B = light from top (+Y), A = opacity (view-projected extinction)

ue_texture.note: do not use TC_Masks/BC1: RGB+A all carry data

niagara.material: 6-way lighting: dot(LightDir_world->camera-space, axes) -> weights max(+/-L.x..z,0) over (R,L,T,B,K,F); sum weights*maps; multiply by albedo colour and light colour; Opacity = map A.A

textures.generator: vfx_smoke: curl-advected looping fBm density volume 128x128x32, Wrenninge multiple-scatter transmittance along 6 axes, projected along view

textures.name: T_VFX_Smoke_6Way_B_8x8
textures.channels_desc: R = light from bottom (-Y), G = light from back (-Z, away from camera), B = light from front (+Z, camera side), A = normalised optical thickness (for backlit translucency / SSS fudge)

niagara.material: 6-way lighting: dot(LightDir_world->camera-space, axes) -> weights max(+/-L.x..z,0) over (R,L,T,B,K,F); sum weights*maps; multiply by albedo colour and light colour; Opacity = map A.A

textures.name: T_VFX_Smoke_BakedTopLit_8x8
textures.channels_desc: RGB = smoke lit from above (sky 1.0) with warm key from upper-left/front, neutral grey albedo 0.45; A = opacity. Use when 6-way is overkill.

niagara.material: Colour = tex.rgb * TintColour; Opacity = tex.a * ParticleAlpha; soft-particle depth fade 20-80 cm; tint dark (0.15-0.3) for house-fire smoke

textures.name: T_VFX_SoftMask_A_256
textures.channels_desc: R = (1-r^2)^2 smooth falloff, G = gaussian exp(-4.5 r^2) windowed, B = linear cone, A = soft ring (r=0.62)

niagara.material: Radial masks for sprite particles, decals, light-cookie-like glows, depth-fade shaping

textures.name: T_VFX_SoftMask_B_256
textures.channels_desc: R = soft superellipse square, G = horizontal streak (4:1), B = vertical edge fade, A = cloudy circle (radial * fBm)

niagara.material: Ground-contact dust shapes, light shafts, streak particles
